kpis.sub: MP SITS AT ITS 52-WEEK LOW AS THE RARE-EARTH SELLOFF DEEPENS (OCT 23 CLOSE)
kpis.label: MP Materials closed $38.30 on Oct 23 (-0.7%), just $0.73 above its $37.57 52-week low and down from ~$40 a week earlier. USAR closed $9.33 (-3.1%), through its prior low and now at the bottom of a $9.26–$32.80 range, and REMX closed $51.46, at the bottom of a $50.62–$111.55 range (-23.8% total return over 12 months). The Nov 5 Q3 report (after the close) is the next company test. MP also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count

kpis.sub: CHINA'S 12-MONTH SUSPENSION OF ITS OCT 2025 RARE-EARTH CONTROLS LAPSES IN 16 DAYS — NO RENEWAL ANNOUNCED
kpis.label: Correction to last week's page: the suspension of Beijing's Oct 9, 2025 controls (five more elements incl. erbium, holmium, europium, plus the 0.1% foreign-content rule) expires Nov 10, 2026, not Jan 10, 2027. The broader US-China trade truce was extended to Jan 10, 2027 (MOFCOM, Sep 28), but that announcement did not name the rare-earth suspension, so the clause is unconfirmed in writing. April 2025 licensing on seven elements stays regardless. Jan–Sep exports were 43,711t (-9.6% YoY) and September magnet shipments to the US fell 28.7% vs August

kpis.sub: LITHIUM CARBONATE DOWN ~27% IN A MONTH, BELOW THE CNY 100,000 LEVEL (OCT 23)
kpis.label: China lithium carbonate fell 2.4% on Oct 23 to CNY 97,000/t, -27% over a month though still +29% year over year, after SMM's revised method added ~175,000t to Chinese inventory estimates and Bald Hill and Finniss restarted. LIT fell 4.0% on Oct 22 and closed $60.68 on Oct 23 (-4% on the week). Albemarle closed $93.67 (+1.2%), near its $88.01 low, with several analysts cutting targets (Citi $125 from $175); Lithium Americas closed $2.07, at its $2.04 low

kpis.sub: COMEX COPPER AT A FIVE-WEEK LOW AS AI-STOCK SELLOFF AND TARIFF-DROP TALK WEIGH (OCT 23–25)
kpis.label: Copper was ~$6.48/lb (futures near $6.40, a five-week low), -3.6% over a month but +27% year over year, versus a $6.85 record in September. Pressures: the AI-stock selloff and speculation the US may drop proposed refined-copper tariffs; strike risk at major miners still supports it. Freeport closed $65.18 on Oct 23 (+0.9%), down from $69.54 a week earlier; Q3 earnings are due Oct 27

themes.title: China's rare-earth suspension expires Nov 10 — the Jan 10 date covers the trade truce, not clearly the controls
themes.description: The 12-month suspension of Beijing's Oct 2025 controls ends Nov 10 with no renewal announced; the Sep 28 extension of the wider truce to Jan 10, 2027 did not name the rare-earth clause. Analysts frame three paths: extend, reinstate selectively against defense/tech users, or reinstate in full. Beijing is offering case-by-case general licences (the EU has begun receiving them) while April 2025 licensing stays. Equities are already near 52-week lows, so the market is pricing a poor outcome, not a resolved one.

themes.title: GM terminated its magnet supply deal with VAC's South Carolina plant — now Energy Fuels' to digest
themes.description: Per Oct 23 reporting, GM cancelled (effective Jul 1) a 2023 long-term supply agreement for e-VAC's ~$500M, ~2,000t/yr South Carolina magnet plant, which had been 90% earmarked for GM; VAC has launched arbitration. Energy Fuels agreed in June to buy VAC for $1.9B and said the price may adjust with the arbitration outcome. The link is GM's EV pullback — a reminder that Western magnet capacity still needs anchor customers, not just policy.

themes.title: Juniors keep funding through equity and mergers while prices stay low
themes.description: Critical Metals filed a securities-offering registration and its European Lithium merger was approved on Oct 22; Energy Fuels' $500M at-the-market programme is still drawing investor-rights law-firm probes, though its ASM acquisition was approved by ASM holders and terbium oxide qualified with a major Japanese magnet maker. USAR's government money remains milestone-based. Backstops favour projects with product.

themes.title: Lynas hits a new low ahead of its Oct 29 quarterly — and the report date was wrong last week
themes.description: Lynas fell 5.9% on Oct 23 to A$10.71, the bottom of its A$10.71–A$22.37 range, ahead of the September-quarter report on Thursday Oct 29 (interim CEO Pol Le Roux hosts the 10am Sydney briefing); last week's page listed Oct 25. Production growth (FY26 revenue A$978M, +76%) is not being rewarded while NdPr prices stay depressed and the Meteoric all-scrip deal adds integration risk.

bear_case.title: The premium keeps deflating faster than the supply chain is built
bear_case.description: Even with a trade truce in place, REMX closed $51.46 on Oct 23 (-23.8% over 12 months), MP is at its 52-week low near $38, USAR broke to $9.33 and Lynas to A$10.71. MP remains loss-making at the EPS line on a high price-to-sales multiple, and the GM/VAC cancellation shows Western magnet capacity can lose anchor demand even with policy support.

bear_case.title: Commodity cycles cut both ways
bear_case.description: Lithium carbonate has fallen ~27% in a month to CNY 97,000/t with Bald Hill and Finniss restarts and a larger Chinese stockpile estimate; Albemarle ($93.67) and Lithium Americas ($2.07) reflect it. Copper slipped to a five-week low near $6.40–6.48/lb on the AI-stock selloff and tariff-drop talk, so Freeport ($65.18) is exposed to a macro unwind even at cycle-high prices. A producer can be an excellent business at the wrong point in its price cycle.

bear_case.title: China can flood, freeze or consolidate
bear_case.description: The suspension of the Oct 2025 controls lapses Nov 10 with no renewal announced, and the Jan 10 truce date does not clearly cover it; April 2025 licensing remains. A flood of cheap Chinese NdPr would undercut non-Chinese producers even with Pentagon price floors, which only protect projects that already have product. Lynas's record output at ~70% of NdPr nameplate shows how depressed prices bite.

bear_case.title: Junior dilution, milestone funding and policy dependency
bear_case.description: Energy Fuels' $500M at-the-market programme and law-firm probes, Critical Metals' new offering registration and going-concern doubt, and USAR's milestone-only federal money show juniors funding through shares. Vault, EXIM, DoD floors and the House package are real but discretionary, and H.R. 4090 still has to clear the Senate.

stance.basis: Weights are a share of a hypothetical 100% sleeve for THIS SECTOR only — not a share of your portfolio. Core and Speculative names carry the weight; Watch and Avoid deliberately carry 0% because the point of those groups is that you are not holding them yet.

positions.name: MP Materials
positions.note: Only US mine-to-magnet producer with Apple and DoD anchors and Q2 revenue up 89% to $108.5M, but at $38.30 (a hair above its $37.57 52-week low) with Q3 due Nov 5 and China's Nov 10 cliff ahead it is held as Core on business quality, not price. Also sits in the Robotics sleeve — don't double-count.

positions.name: USA Rare Earth
positions.note: Blacksburg construction and the Serra Verde deal are real and Texas Capital initiated at Buy, but at $9.33 (new 52-week low, -31%+ in a month) with milestone-based federal funding ahead and China's export listing, this is optionality with a genuine chance of zero.

positions.name: Lithium Americas
positions.note: Thacker Pass is still the largest US lithium build, but at $2.07 (at its $2.04 low) with lithium carbonate down ~27% in a month to CNY 97k/t and mechanical completion not until late 2027, the size stays the smallest in the sleeve.

positions.name: Freeport-McMoRan
positions.note: Excellent copper business, but copper slipped to a five-week low (~$6.40–6.48/lb) on the AI-stock selloff and tariff-drop talk and the shares ($65.18) trade with the tape ahead of Oct 27 earnings — a late-cycle price with an unresolved tariff decision, not an entry point.

positions.name: Albemarle
positions.note: Lithium carbonate fell ~27% in a month to CNY 97k/t on restarts and a larger Chinese stockpile estimate; with ALB at $93.67 near its $88.01 low and analysts cutting targets (Citi $125 from $175), the cycle has not clearly bottomed, and Q3 on Nov 4 plus a new CEO in Feb 2027 leave questions open.

positions.name: Lynas Rare Earths

positions.name: Energy Fuels

positions.name: Critical Metals
